name_reason: Name fully complies. Prefix data_fd2_ correct for a game global. 'ch22' is a meaningful chapter ID (chapters are 1-30) not an address residue. 'end_scene_char_pos_x_table' accurately reflects both purpose (chapter-22 end-scene per-char X positions) and data type (table/array). No Ghidra address residue. Consistent with all sibling end-scene x-tables in chend2.c (ch20/21/23/26/27/30).
purpose: Chapter 22 end-scene per-char-slot world-tile X coordinates; copied onto stack and passed as pos_x arg to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro to place chars 0..15.
logic_summary: fd2_chapter_22_end @ 0x244B6 prologue copies this 16-byte table (REP MOVSD x4 dwords, ESI=0x52273) plus its y-table (0x52283) and facing-table (0x52293) onto stack scratch, then passes the three stack pointers as arg1/arg2/arg3 (pos_x/pos_y/facing) to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro, which indexes each by char slot. The handler then runs post-battle dialog pages 4/5/6 with cutscene events 0x41/0x42 and the FD2-unique white->black fade ending. This table supplies the X coordinate per char slot.
element_semantics: element[i] = world-tile X coordinate for end-scene char slot i (i = 0..15). Values range 0x14..0x18.
notes: Memory @ 0x52273 (16 bytes) = 16 16 15 17 14 15 16 17 18 14 15 16 17 18 15 17, byte-identical to the C array in chend2.c lines 268-271. Only xref is fd2_chapter_22_end (READ @ 0x244d3, DATA @ 0x244ce); zero writers confirms const. Home-file comment block (chend2.c lines 260-267) was already accurate and precise (states addresses, read-only, single reader, dword-copy-to-stack prologue mechanism, facing-table uniformity note); left unchanged. Ghidra data plate was NULL; created a concise plate via run_script_inline+PLATE_COMMENT reflecting the src conclusion (verified written). No src edit made; only shard added.
